newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Syria's Assad says Israel destroys peace process.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad says Israel destroys peace process.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad said in a U.S. television interview that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appears to be "obliterating" peace commitments made by the previous Israeli Labour government.

"Once the results of the Israeli elections were announced, the new Israeli Prime Minister appeared to be obliterating all the principles and eliminating all efforts, commitments and rights. And so he cancelled the peace process entirely," Assad told CNN International in an interview to be aired on Saturday.

"Talks can only be resumed once he (Netanyahu) makes up his mind on the peace strategy and on responding to its requirements," Assad said in the interview held on Wednesday in Damascus. Excerpts were made available by CNN on Friday.
Assad said that stability in the Middle East would diminish if negotiations were not resumed between Israel and Syria and such a situation could lead to war.
"Changes in this stability could lead to what we may call war or wars," he said.
But Assad, in his first U.S. and European television interview since 1993, said that the peace process was not dead but only "stumbling."

In Israel, clashes broke out on Wednesday as Palestinians protested against Israel's opening of a tunnel that runs near holy Moslem sites in Jerusalem. By Friday, 53 Palestinians and 14 Israelis had been killed in the worst outbreak of violence since Israel and the Palestinians signed a peace accord in 1993.

Assad disclosed after years of public denials that Israel's former Labour government and Syria, in four years of negotiations, had reached an agreement on Israeli withdrawal from the Syrian Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the June 1967 war.
Netanyahu won May elections on a platform opposed to trading occupied Arab land for peace.

"Agreement was reached between Syria and Israel on Israeli withdrawal from the Golan up to June 4, 1967 lines. After that we moved to complete discussion of the other elements of peace. And all that took place under the supervision and with the knowledge of the United States," he said.
No peace talks have been held between Israel and Syria since the May election of Netanyahu as prime minister.
Syria, which has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991, wants Netanyahu to announce readiness to withdraw fully from the Golan ahead of any resumption of negotiations.
Assad said Netanyahu was to be judged in the light of his words and deeds."

"In the light of what we heard of his statements, he is blocking the road towards peace, because he himself has said, for example, that he would not give back the rights and the land of Palestinians, and would not return the Golan to Syria."

"If this is how he thinks, then why should Syria want peace? can any sensible man in the world expect Syria to make peace with the Israeli government while Syrian territory remains occupied by the Israelis?" he said.
Assad denied that a recent Syrian troop movement from the Bekaa valley in Lebanon closer to the Golan Heights amounted in any way to an attack on Israel.
He reiterated his denial that Palestinian groups based in Syria were involved in violent attacks against Israel.

"Those who are now in Syria do not commit any act of violence from inside Syria. If there are such acts, they are inside Palestine, and not in Syria. And those who carry them out inside Palestinian territory are not those who live in Syria."
